summary: Dedicated capacity throughput degradation causing increased latency and timeouts for NovaChat (noisy neighbor / GPU contention)
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (NovaChat) reported a sustained throughput degradation and elevated request timeouts (5-10% timeouts) on their dedicated GPU pool that started on 2026-02-20 03:15 UTC. Impact: increased tail latency (p95 to p99), failed streaming sessions, and request timeouts causing user-visible errors.

Impact:
- Customer-facing latency regressions (p95 increased from ~120ms to ~450ms; p99 spiking to multiple seconds).
- ~5-10% of requests returned 524/timeout errors during the incident window.
- Affects production workload for NovaChat pinned to dedicated pool: redwood-dedicated-novachat-us-east.

Environment:
- Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool) in us-east-1
- Models in use: redwood/3b-chat (default), fallback to open/llama-2-13b-chat
- Autoscaler config: min_nodes=2, max_nodes=8, scale_policy=cpu_and_queue (legacy config)

Steps to reproduce / observed behavior:
1) Customer traffic pattern: bursty parallel chat sessions at 03:10-03:25 UTC.
2) Serving runtime queue length increases; scheduler shows high packer imbalance and GPU runqueue pile-up.
3) Tail latency rises and requests begin timing out after 30s streaming wait.
4) Some requests were routed to fallback model variants; routing fallbacks also experienced degraded perf.

Relevant logs / metrics:
- Autoscaler events show only one scale-up from 2->3 nodes at 03:18 UTC; further scale-ups delayed until 03:30 despite sustained queue depth.
- GPU utilization on one node at 98-100% with high SM saturation and increasing memory bandwidth wait.
- NVLink/Aggregate interconnect metrics show high peer-to-peer contention on the affected node.
- Serving runtime traces indicate frequent context-switches and longer KV-cache misses on affected GPUs.
- No config changes by customer at the time of incident (confirmed via customer).

Initial hypothesis:
- Noisy neighbor: a co-located job on the same physical host caused GPU contention and high PCIe/NVLink saturation.
- Autoscaler mis-sizing/slow reaction: legacy scale policy did not respond quickly to sudden burst, causing sustained overload on a small number of nodes.
- Pod packing/scheduler affinity allowed multiple high-throughput pods to land on the same GPU host.
investigation_notes: 2026-02-20 03:25 UTC - Support received first alert from NovaChat about timeouts; escalated to SRE and serving-runtime.
2026-02-20 03:30 UTC - SRE checked autoscaler logs: only one scale-up occurred (2->3). Queue depth still high; autoscaler decision window showed low CPU-based signals due to GPU-bound workload.

2026-02-20 03:35 UTC - Observed one physical host (node-ue1-57) with two high-throughput pods: novachat-infer-1 and third-party-batch-job-72. GPU metrics showed SM utilization ~98%, high memory bandwidth contention, and elevated NVLink traffic. This matched noisy-neighbor symptoms.

2026-02-20 03:40 UTC - Correlated request traces: requests routed to node-ue1-57 had 3-7x higher decode latency compared to other nodes. KV cache hit rate lower on that node coinciding with context-switch events.
2026-02-20 03:45 UTC - Support requested immediate mitigation: cordon/drain node-ue1-57 and reschedule novachat pods. Also triggered manual scale-up to 6 nodes to relieve pressure.
2026-02-20 03:52 UTC - After evacuation and manual scale-up, p95 latency reduced back to ~140ms and timeouts dropped to <0.5%. Customer confirmed improvement.

2026-02-21 09:00 UTC - Post-incident analysis: scheduler packing policy allowed non-isolated batch jobs in the same GPU rack; autoscaler used CPU/queue metrics which underrepresented GPU saturation for these workloads.

2026-02-22 11:15 UTC - Identified related infra PR that changed node labelling behavior earlier in February; reviewed PR for unexpected packing changes (linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/scheduler/pull/611).
2026-02-22 14:00 UTC - Cross-team sync with scheduler, autoscaler, and serving-runtime to propose mitigations and follow-ups.

resolution_summary:
Immediate mitigation: cordoned and drained affected host (node-ue1-57) and manually scaled the dedicated pool from 2->6 nodes; rescheduled NovaChat pods across isolated hosts. Result: p95 reduced to ~140ms, timeouts dropped below SLA. Root cause: noisy neighbor (co-located high-throughput batch job) plus autoscaler configuration that relied on CPU/queue signals and under-reacted to GPU saturation.

Permanent fixes implemented/planned:
- Scheduler: enforce isolation labels for dedicated pools and update packer heuristics to avoid co-locating heavy jobs with customer-dedicated pods (rolled to staging on 2026-02-22).
- Autoscaler: add GPU-utilization and GPU-queue depth signals to scale policy and adjust decision window to be more responsive to bursty traffic (PR opened, targeting canary on 2026-03-01).
- Monitoring/alerts: added alert for sustained GPU SM utilization > 90% for 5 minutes and queue backlog > threshold.
- Runbook: updated dedicated capacity runbook with noisy-neighbor mitigation steps, autoscaler tuning guidance, and customer communication template.

Follow-ups assigned: scheduler team, autoscaler team, and SRE to verify canary metrics and run a synthetic burst test with NovaChat before closing monitoring follow-ups.
